decision.title: The XML and XHTML output methods (packet )
decision.summary: The serializer splits into parts, and src/serialize_xml.c implements the XML and XHTML methods: character pipeline, pull-based sequence normalization, namespace declarations, indentation, XHTML and Canonical XML rules.

body.p: as a second (4.3 has ); renamed at the Phase 2 gate (). src/serialize_internal.h splits the serializer into parts: src/serialize.c keeps the output stream and buffer, the parameter checks, the character pipeline, sequence normalization, the adaptive method and the dispatch; src/serialize_xml.c has the XML and XHTML methods and the node writer the adaptive method uses. Packet 's HTML, text, JSON and CSV parts build on the same internal interface.

item.p: Dispatch ( follow-up): HTML, text, JSON and CSV return UNSUPPORTED_FEATURE until 3.4; parameters C can say but XDM cannot (enumerations out of range, ill-formed UTF-8, name 0, a character map codepoint twice or not an XML Char) are INVALID_ARGUMENT for every method; indent-unit, doctype-system, doctype-public and html-version values the spec forbids are SEPM0016.

Character pipeline (Serialization 4.0, section 4): sxml_serializer writes markup, text, attribute values, URI attribute values and CDATA sections. Text and attribute values go through the character map (sorted once, binary search), then sxml_unicode_normalize (; the serialize.h form maps onto unicode_internal.h's, fully-normalized as NFC plus SERE0012 for a construct that starts with a composing character) on each unmapped segment, then escaping, line endings and the encoding into a 512-byte staging area. References are &#xHEX;; C0 and C1 controls, NEL and LINE SEPARATOR are always references in text and attributes (also with version 1.0: XML 1.1's repertoire, QT4 K2-Serialization-7, Serialization-xml-27 to -31); a character the encoding lacks is a reference there and SERE0008 in markup. UTF-16 is big endian; byte-order-mark writes EF BB BF or FE FF.

Sequence normalization is a pull iterator (sxml_sequence_normalizer) that never builds the result tree: frames flatten arrays and JNode values, atomic items are cast to text joined by a space or the item separator, documents give their children, text is merged in a heap buffer. SEPM0004 (doctype-system or standalone with text or several elements at the top) runs the iterator once more first.

Namespaces: each element's declarations are computed against a stack of written bindings: its in-scope namespaces (minus xml) plus what its own and its attributes' names need, declared where the written bindings differ, xmlns="" where a default goes out of scope, and xmlns:p="" only with undeclare-prefixes and version 1.1 (SEPM0010 with 1.0). XHTML with HTML5 applies prefix normalization (XHTML, SVG, MathML elements unprefixed; their prefixes dropped unless an attribute of an ancestor-or-self uses them, Issue 2821). Canonical XML uses the same rule (it is C14N 1.1's namespace axis) and sorts declarations and attributes by heapsort (no recursion, O(n log n)).

Indentation (5.1.4, 6.1.5): an element's content is indented only when it has element, comment or PI children and no text other than whitespace, its name is not in suppress-indentation (XHTML: also without regard to case), it has no xml:space="preserve", it is not a formatted or inline HTML element and has no inline child, and its parent is indented itself, so nothing below mixed or suppressed content moves. Whitespace-only text is dropped where whitespace is added. indent-unit defaults to two spaces; indent-attributes puts each further attribute on its own line. Newlines between top-level nodes and after the declaration only when indenting; none otherwise (QT4 Serialization-xml-01, -xhtml-72).

XHTML (section 6): html-version defaults to 5.0; minimized tags only for elements expected to be empty (
with HTML5,
before),

otherwise; before an html document element with HTML5 and no doctype-system; include-content-type (default yes) adds (HTML5) or the http-equiv form (media type text/html by default) as head's first child and drops existing charset or Content-Type meta children; escape-uri-attributes (default yes) applies URI escaping to the attributes of appendix D.

Canonical XML: UTF-8, LF, no declaration, doctype, CDATA, character maps or indentation; start-end tag pairs; line feeds around nodes outside the document element; SERE0024 for top-level text, more or fewer than one element, or a relative namespace URI.
Adaptive nodes () are written by the same XML writer with the default parameters; a stored parentless namespace node () is written from its name (the prefix) and content (the URI).

Not done here: sxml_serialization_parameter_reader (declared by ) has no definition yet; it belongs with fn:serialize (3.4). Not checked: SERE0005/SERE0006 (names and characters of the XML version), comments with "--" (SERE0003). The CLI's --method stays adaptive until 3.12.
